subject: Disability Pride and Culture Day Fair Planning
overview: The Commission finalized logistical arrangements for the May 9 Disability Pride and Culture Day fair and discussed ongoing municipal accessibility initiatives. Members reviewed vendor participation, facility accessibility requirements, and the extension of digital compliance deadlines.

items.title: Meeting Minutes Approval
items.summary: Approved the minutes from the previous meeting with a correction to the date of a recent site visit.

items.title: Fair Logistics and Accessibility
items.summary: Discussed venue layouts for the McGlynn School and planned accommodations including a designated quiet room, accessible seating, and non-fluorescent lighting.

items.title: Vendor and Performance Coordination
items.summary: Confirmed over 20 participating organizations and selected musical selections for inclusive dance performances.

items.title: Mayoral Proclamation and Commission Speaker
items.summary: Announced a proclamation declaring May 9 as Disability Pride and Culture Day and designated Commissioner Joe Casey to deliver a speech on behalf of the body.

items.title: Police Department Sponsorship and Training
items.summary: Discussed the police department's role as the performance sponsor and debated the effectiveness of law enforcement interaction training for people with disabilities.

items.title: Grants and Digital Accessibility Updates
items.summary: Reviewed a municipal grant for ADA self-evaluation and announced that the city's deadline for digital accessibility compliance has been extended to 2027.

items.title: Accessible Infrastructure and Trees
items.summary: Examined the importance of planting accessible tree species that do not damage sidewalks or create tripping hazards.

items.title: Interactive Activities and Community Events
items.summary: Proposed interactive polling activities for the fair and highlighted upcoming local events including a youth summit and Haitian Flag Day.
